reasoning: Recent high-quality polling and averages show Ohio’s 2026 Senate race between Democrat Sherrod Brown and Republican Jon Husted effectively a toss-up, but with a slight Republican edge in the overall polling average. The clearest quantified read is Pollsmax’s statewide Senate polling average of R+2.8 as of July 6, 2026, while other syntheses (VoteHub, NYT issue-poll piece) suggest a race that has swung from a small GOP lead to roughly even or very slight D edge, so the best current summary is that the Senate margin is approximately R+2–3 statewide. Given Ohio’s underlying R+6 Cook PVI, this confirms a structurally Republican-leaning state with a genuinely competitive but modestly R-tinted Senate contest at the moment.

sources.name: The New York Times/Siena College
sources.details: New York Times/Siena poll of Ohio’s U.S. Senate race found Jon Husted leading Sherrod Brown 50%–47%, a margin of R+3, indicating a narrow Republican advantage within the margin of error.

sources.name: AARP / Impact Research & Fabrizio Ward
sources.details: AARP-sponsored bipartisan poll by Impact Research and Fabrizio Ward found Sherrod Brown leading Jon Husted 48%–45%, a margin of D+3, underscoring that the race is highly competitive with small, opposing leads across polls.

sources.name: Fox News / Beacon Research & Shaw & Company
sources.details: Fox News–commissioned Beacon Research/Shaw & Company poll showed Sherrod Brown ahead of Jon Husted 53%–45%, a margin of D+8, an outlier more favorable to Democrats compared with other surveys.

sources.name: Tulchin Research
sources.details: Tulchin Research poll reported Sherrod Brown leading Jon Husted 46%–42%, a D+4 margin in the Senate race, again pointing to a narrow but plausible Democratic edge in some polling.

sources.name: Echelon Insights / NetChoice
sources.details: Echelon Insights poll for NetChoice found Jon Husted ahead of Sherrod Brown 51%–45%, an R+6 margin, consistent with Ohio’s right-leaning fundamentals.

sources.name: Pollsmax (Ohio Senate polling average)
sources.details: Pollsmax’s 2026 Ohio Senate polling average (Brown vs. Husted) shows 45.1% D to 47.9% R, an overall margin of R+2.8, providing the clearest quantified statewide margin as of early July.
sources.date_range: July 6, 2026 (polling average as of that date, covering multiple 2026 polls)

sources.name: Newsweek summarizing VoteHub Ohio Senate average
sources.details: VoteHub’s polling average cited by Newsweek indicates the Ohio Senate race moved from an R+0.3 edge in April to D+0.9 by July 20, suggesting a slight Democratic lead but still essentially a toss-up.
sources.date_range: April 20–July 20, 2026 (comparison of April vs. July averages)

sources.name: Daily Kos summarizing recent Ohio Senate polling & Cook rating
sources.details: Daily Kos analysis notes that, averaging four post–May 5 primary polls, Sherrod Brown leads Jon Husted by about 3 points in the Senate race, while also describing wide variation from Husted+3 to Brown+8; it further reports Cook Political Report rating the Ohio Senate contest as a toss-up.

sources.name: Newsweek / VoteHub (Ohio Senate toss-up & markets)
sources.details: Newsweek’s “VoteHub” piece again reports Ohio’s Senate polling average as D+0.9 by July 20 and notes prediction markets giving each party roughly even chances, reinforcing that the race is a true toss-up.

sources.name: The New York Times (multi-state Senate polling analysis)
sources.details: A New York Times Senate polling analysis lists Ohio as Brown +2 / Husted −1 in its issue-alignment metrics, implying a very slight Democratic edge in its synthesized view of recent Senate polling.
sources.date_range: July 14, 2026 (issue-poll analysis drawing on recent surveys)

sources.name: Cook Political Report (statewide Ohio PVI, referenced)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s statewide Partisan Voting Index rates Ohio at R+6, indicating the state votes about six points more Republican than the national average; this is a structural measure, not a 2026 race poll.
sources.date_range: Cook PVI as of the 2024 cycle, applied to 2026 context
